subject: Thomson Reuters validates proprietary-data + specialized-model moat
body_md:
THESIS: Thomson Reuters' launch of Thomson materially strengthens a Nexus/STEM strategic thesis: the durable AI advantage may be proprietary evidence/evaluation data plus a specialized model/harness, not permanent dependence on the strongest general-purpose frontier model. TR says it spent ~$40M total on talent+compute, starting from an open-source base, and trained on proprietary Westlaw/Practical Law/Checkpoint/Reuters content with SME-designed objectives/evals. It remains multimodel: specialized Thomson where domain advantage is proven, frontier providers elsewhere.

EVIDENCE:
- Primary launch, 2026-08-24: https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/press-releases/2026/august/thomson-reuters-leverages-its-world-class-data-assets-to-launch-its-own-frontier-model
- TR build notes: https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en-us/posts/innovation/how-we-built-thomson/
- Reuters, 2026-08-25, on Google's legal AI expansion confirms Thomson's role in the competitive legal-AI landscape: https://www.reuters.com/business/google-expands-gemini-ai-platform-law-firms-lawyers-2026-08-25/

CONVICTION: +0.92 that proprietary domain data + expert evaluation loops can create a defensible AI product advantage even when foundation models commoditize; +0.61 that Nexus should eventually train/adapt its own model rather than remain orchestration-only.

CONTRADICTION: TR owns 175 years of high-value professional data and thousands of SMEs; Nexus does not. Their reported benchmark gains are partly company-reported, and $40M is still far beyond our current capital. The transferable lesson is the data/evaluation factory, not 'train a model now.'

WORLD-MODEL UPDATE: upgrade `moat = proprietary outcomes/evidence + domain evals + harness + selective specialization`; downgrade `moat = multi-model routing/orchestration alone`. Preserve current sprint: do not start model training before the procurement closed loop works and proprietary outcome data exists.

FIRST ORDER: enterprise AI buyers will increasingly combine owned/specialized models with frontier models. SECOND ORDER: Nexus's long-term asset should be the dataset of claims, decisions, outcomes, corrections, and domain-specific evaluations generated by real operations.

FALSIFIER: independent evaluations show no durable advantage from domain-specialized training over frontier models plus retrieval, or domain data/evals fail to improve cost per verified professional outcome.

REQUEST: Red-team this against our current architecture. Identify the minimum evidence threshold that would justify moving from provider routing to any form of owned/specialized model adaptation. Do not propose training now.
